head.name: @fzlt/core/slot
head.lead: Mount a Fizlet scene into an Astro page engine slot: the element carrying class="ae-slot" data-slot-target="<page>#<slot>" role="img" aria-label="…". Both shapes the engine has rendered are found: the figure itself (<figure class="ae-slot">), or a box inside one (<figure class="ae-slot-figure"><div class="ae-slot">…</div><figcaption class="ae-slot__fallback">, where the caption sits outside the role="img" box and stays: it is not over the scene). - Lazy: nothing loads or runs until the slot comes near the viewport, and then only once the main thread is idle (or idle ms have passed), so the page's own work goes first. - Safe first tap: a tap on the slot before the scene is up loads it at once and is handed to the scene as plain numbers (first), never as a stale PointerEvent whose pointer is gone. - Reduced motion: the slot keeps its placeholder and fallback; the scene never loads. If the setting turns on while a scene runs, the scene goes and the fallback comes back. - Accessible: role="img" + aria-label stay unless the scene says it renders real accessible content (accessible: true): then role="img" becomes role="figure" (a <figure>'s own role, so the label stays on a role that takes one) in place, and Recall puts "img" back in the same spot, byte for byte. Until then the stage is aria-hidden. - Contained: the scene gets its own stage inside the slot (contain: strict). Every change the slot makes goes through a Ledger, so destroy() gives the page back exactly. - Off screen, off the page's frame: the stage is content-visibility: auto, so a scene scrolled away is skipped for style, layout, paint and layers. Without it a 3D scene's composited layers stayed in every repaint elsewhere on the page (Chromium layerizes the whole document).
